title: PPE beyond box-ticking: how to check protection before work
description: Helmet, goggles, gloves and respirator provide protection only when they are suitable for the task, are in good working order and are worn correctly.

blocks.content: Personal protective equipment is the last barrier between danger and a person. It does not correct a faulty machine or replace a guard, but can reduce the consequences if selected for a specific risk and used correctly.
Five questions before you wear PPE

items: What danger does it protect against in this particular task?
Is the model and protection class suitable for the material, tool and conditions?
Is the size correct and can the fit be adjusted?
Are there any cracks, tears, dirt, expired or missing parts?
Do I know the limitations and signs when the protection needs to be replaced?

blocks.title: “On me” does not mean “protects”
blocks.content: An unsuitable filter, an unfastened helmet, a scratched visor or oversized gloves create a false sense of security. If you are in doubt about the choice or fit, check before starting work.

rows: Case without cracks or strong dents; the internal equipment is intact; fit adjusted
Lenses provide clear vision; no cracks; temples or strap hold glasses
Material suitable for risk; no punctures or tears; size does not interfere with grip
Filter type corresponds to hazard; fit checked; valves and belts are OK
The sole is intact and clean; the toe is not deformed; lacing or clasps are in good condition
blocks.caption: What to see before your shift

blocks.content: If the glasses fog up, the helmet slips, and the glove clings to parts, the person begins to adjust or remove the protection. This is a signal not to “endure”, but to choose a size, adjustment or compatible model. Several PPE should work together: the temples of the glasses should not interfere with the fit of the respirator, and the hood should not interfere with the fastening of the helmet.

items: after an impact, fall or contact with a substance if this could damage the protection;
in case of crack, rupture, deformation, loss of transparency or failure of fastening;
if the filter has exhausted its service life or there is an odor, breathing resistance or other signs according to the manufacturer’s instructions;
if PPE cannot be cleaned properly or has been stored incorrectly;
if the operation or hazard has changed and the current protection is not intended for them.

blocks.content: The calendar period is not permission to use the damaged item. Report the defect and receive a serviceable replacement in the manner established at your workplace. Do not repair the protector with tape, glue or random parts unless such repairs are provided by the manufacturer.

blocks.title: Good habit
blocks.content: Inspect PPE twice: before use and after use. A second inspection helps spot damage early rather than at the start of the next urgent task.
